name: Bank and finance
purpose: anti-money laundering and know your customer checks, fraud and scams, conduct and market abuse, mis-selling and suitability, customer vulnerability, dual control and secure access, data protection

identity.place: The head office and main branch of a regional bank (about 600 staff) in a cathedral city: a five-storey 1930s steel-framed building faced in pale cream limestone on a corner of the main street. The ground floor is the old banking hall, still the main branch: about 18 m deep, 10 m across and 6.0 m high to a coffered plaster ceiling, with the interview rooms opening off its far end. The strong room is in the basement below it. The upper floors were refitted in 2019: the financial crime team works on the third floor and the treasury dealing room is on the fourth.
architecture: the street walls: tall windows in deep limestone reveals; in the banking hall each is 2.0 m wide and 3.8 m high with its sill at 1.2 m, on the upper floors 1.6 m wide and 2.0 m high with the sill at 0.85 m; all have slim bronze-coloured metal frames divided by one mullion and three transoms into eight tall panes (two across, four up), never small square panes

the banking hall: walls lined to 2.8 m in cream plaster jointed to look like large limestone blocks, plain cream plaster above; shallow pilasters between the windows; a coffered plaster ceiling at 6.0 m; opal glass globe pendants on long bronze-coloured rods; a polished cream terrazzo floor with a border of burgundy and grey bands

the counter: a run of cashier positions along one side of the hall, a walnut-veneer front and a pale stone-coloured top at 1.05 m, a clear glass screen from the counter top to 2.2 m with a speech panel and a recessed deal tray at each position, low glass dividers between positions; one low position at 0.85 m with a knee recess; the staff side behind it is closed by the hall's side wall

the strong room in the basement: painted concrete walls, a heavy rectangular steel door in a steel frame set into a thick concrete wall, a steel bar day gate inside the door, and a room lined with safe deposit boxes

the refitted upper floors: a smooth white plaster ceiling at 3.0 m with recessed linear lights, square columns 0.5 m wide cased in white on an 8 by 6 m grid, charcoal carpet tiles (on a raised floor in the dealing room), walnut-veneer doors in bronze-coloured frames, glass meeting rooms with frosted bands
the interview rooms: small private rooms off the banking hall, solid walls (no glass fronts, for privacy), each with one street window
identity.materials: cream limestone and cream plaster, polished cream terrazzo, walnut veneer, bronze-coloured metal (window frames, pendant rods, door frames, handles), burgundy as the bank's colour (a painted wall panel, chair upholstery, queue belts, carpet borders), charcoal and pale grey upholstery, clear and frosted glass, black screens; signal red only on the few things that are red in life (a fire extinguisher, a fire alarm call point)
inhabited: paper still matters: blank leaflets in a wall rack, a stack of plain envelopes, a clipboard, case files with coloured tabs (no words), a pen on a coiled cord at the counter

security in plain sight: PIN pads on short swivel stands, lanyards and badges on every member of staff (drawn on chairs and desks here), a locked pedestal under each desk, a small black dome camera on a ceiling
personal things allowed on a clear desk: a mug, a water bottle, a small plant, a cardigan on a chair back; never loose papers left out overnight

the infrastructure of a working bank: a fire extinguisher on its bracket, a green first-aid box, a hearing loop pictogram on the counter glass (a blue ear, no letters), cable trays under the dealing desks
slight wear: the terrazzo dulled along the walk to the counter, a queue belt sagging a little, a chair with a lower back than the others
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall: the banking hall's ceiling is at 6.0 m, 3.4 times a person's height; the upper floors' ceilings are at 3.0 m; a door is 2.1 m high and 0.9 m wide
the counter top is at 1.05 m for standing customers and 0.85 m at the one low position; the glass screen rises to 2.2 m; a cashier's tall chair has its seat at 0.75 m
desks are 1.6 by 0.8 m at 0.72 m; an interview table is 1.4 by 0.8 m at 0.73 m; a seat is 0.45 m high
a dealer's desk is 1.6 m wide and 0.9 m deep with six 24 inch screens (each about 0.54 by 0.32 m) in two rows of three on a two-tier arm, the top row's upper edge at about 1.5 m
the strong room door's clear opening is 0.9 m wide and 2.0 m high, its steel leaf about 0.3 m thick; safe deposit box fronts are 5 by 10 inches (0.13 by 0.25 m) and multiples of it
a fire extinguisher hangs on a bracket with its handle about 1 m above the floor; green exit signs with a running figure and an arrow (no words) sit above exit doors at about 2.3 m
identity.default_light: Late morning on a clear winter day. The street walls face north-west, so no direct sun comes in at this hour: bright, soft, slightly cool daylight falls in through the tall windows and fades across the deep rooms. In the banking hall the opal globe pendants are on and warm; on the upper floors the recessed linear lights are on, a neutral white. Shadows are soft and short and fall away from the windows.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the tall eight-pane window with its slim bronze-coloured frame in a deep cream reveal, cream limestone or limestone-jointed plaster, polished cream terrazzo or a burgundy and grey border band, one burgundy element (a wall panel, upholstery, a queue belt), walnut veneer, an opal glass globe or a bronze-coloured fitting.
avoid: a cartoon bank: no columns of gold bars, no money bags with dollar signs, no piles of coins, no round sci-fi vault doors
exposed brick, small-paned steel factory windows, birch ply, brass desk lamps or deep green (they belong to another place)
real brands, logos, signs with words, currency symbols, flags or anything that pins a country
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
words or numbers on screens, papers, leaflets or signs (empty slots only)
screens facing a window or with a window directly behind them: screens sit at about 90 degrees to the windows
sun patches (the street walls face north-west and the hour is late morning)
a catalogue-clean bank: every scene shows that people work here
identity.outside: Through the windows: the cream stone and brick fronts of the main street's other buildings, shop awnings without words, a bare tree and a pale winter sky; on the upper floors, roofs and, far off, the top of a cathedral tower drawn plainly (no recognisable building).

cast.role: a cashier (bank teller) at the counter
a financial adviser or account manager in the interview rooms
a branch colleague or manager who walks the hall and helps at the counter
financial crime analysts (AML, sanctions, fraud), several, varied in age and background
dealers in the treasury dealing room, and a compliance officer who walks it
customers, including a vulnerable older customer and a bereaved customer, drawn with dignity
a fraudster (ordinary looking; never a cartoon villain), often only a voice on a phone

core: safe deposit box and its two keys
common: cash in a plain band (no currency marks)

research: Real-space facts checked on 2026-10-15 (accessible counter heights: New Zealand, Australian, Indian banking and Texas accessibility guidance; strong room doors, dual control, day gates and time locks: an estimating reference, one bank's written vault procedure and trade summaries; safe deposit box sizes and guard keys: bank pages and a trade article; dealing desks: a trading-desk patent). Sources and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-finance.md.

scenes.light: Late morning on a clear winter day; the street wall faces north-west, so no sun comes in. Bright, soft, slightly cool daylight comes from the left through the tall windows and falls across the hall: the window side of every post, figure and the counter front is brighter and cooler, the right side softer; shadows are short and soft and fall to the right. The opal globes are on and warm, lighting the far wall and the ceiling's coffers gently from within. The terrazzo shows a faint, soft reflection of the windows and the counter front. The glass screen shows a few pale reflections of the windows (thin vertical streaks), never hiding the cashier. Haze about 0.15 on the far wall.
